claim: The repository executed seal-first blinded external validation relative to repository outcome access for the frozen 2024 G2F target.
The 2024 evaluation was calendar-time prospective before the outcomes became public.
The B12 420-cell primary confirmatory cohort completed and failed calibration.
The B12 387-cell available-case cohort supplied diagnostic negative evidence for interval transport.
The 2023 target was unevaluable under the frozen T1 information interface because admissible exact planting dates were unavailable.
The 2024 source compatibility gate admitted a frozen 798-cell prediction universe before outcome access.
B14B sealed 798 predictions with SHA-256 91c765ea994f557db1911865309bca94ebc2110b87a5fea483a03c879d1fb19d before repository access to the observed 2024 yield object.
The B14C primary observable sealed-key cohort contains 779 cells across 19 environments and 92 genotypes.
On B14C the frozen G+E_T1 point predictor achieved RMSE 2.6197348509 and R2 0.1484401927.
The frozen B11 90% interval rule passed the inherited 2024 calibration criterion with environment-balanced coverage 0.8997721030.
The one-sided carry-forward drift guard failed the inherited 2024 calibration criterion with environment-balanced coverage 0.9521031534 and worse mean interval score than the frozen control.
Case Study B establishes a general monotone or nonmonotone law of seasonal calibration error.
The direction of the previous observed calibration error was not sufficiently transport-stable to justify the predeclared one-sided next-season correction in this frozen sequence.
B15 introduces a new calibration-transport or feedback-decision method.
B16 shows mixed 2024 error structure including environment offsets, within-environment error, weak-to-moderate genotype ordering and prediction under-dispersion.
B16 establishes a new error-decomposition methodology.
For the deployed additive G+E architecture the environmental main effect cancels from same-environment genotype contrasts in exact arithmetic.
B17 establishes a new response-amplitude transport method or contraction theorem.
B18 establishes a new forecast-time GxE methodology.
B18 found three direct primary-prior-art collisions and zero surviving novel formal objects, so model development inside B18 was rejected.
Case Study B validates support-based abstention as a selective-risk mechanism.
Case Study B introduces a new state-of-the-art GxE predictive architecture.
T2 was reopened after closure.
B18 automatically authorizes B19 model development.
The central publication contribution is seal-first blinded external-validation discipline, failure preservation, reproducible provenance and hostile novelty termination rather than a new estimator.
